mainTopic: Whether טומאה cancels קידוש ידים ורגלים, dipping inside the כיור, and when the כיור's water becomes disqualified
overview: The amud opens by trying to prove from the פרה אדומה that טומאה does not cancel a כהן's קידוש ידים ורגלים, since the כהן who burns the פרה is made טמא on purpose. The גמרא rejects the proof: the פרה is special, because even a טבול יום may perform it. The washing there is required only so that it resembles Temple service. Next comes a new question: may a כהן wash by dipping his hands and feet inside the כיור, or must the water come out of it? רב נחמן בר יצחק tries to prove from a ברייתא about cave water that dipping is fine, but the גמרא shows the ברייתא had its own reason to mention cave water. Then רבי חייא בר יוסף, רב חסדא and רבי יוחנן give three views on when water left in the כיור becomes disqualified. The גמרא explains רבי יוחנן's rule in light of another teaching in his name, from אילפא. It ends by noting that this makes רבי יוחנן's view identical to רבי חייא בר יוסף's, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A proof from the red heifer that impurity does not cancel the washing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פרה אדומה as proof: the כהן is deliberately made טמא after washing, yet he still performs the service. So טומאה does not cancel קידוש ידים ורגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the red heifer: we deliberately make the priest impure. As the משנה teaches, they would make the priest who burns the heifer impure and then immerse him, to counter the צדוקים, who said the heifer could only be done by someone whose sun had already set. Learn from this that impurity does not disqualify the washing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer its open question with a proof. In the case of the פרה אדומה the כהן becomes טמא on purpose, and the service still goes ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן already washed his hands and feet, and then he is made טמא. Nobody asks him to wash again, so it seems that טומאה does not undo the washing. The משנה explains why they did this on purpose: to publicly reject the view of the צדוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer (פרה אדומה), burned to make ashes for purifying people from contact with the dead
They make someone impure
The Sadducees, a group who rejected the חכמים' tradition
People whose sun has set after immersing, so they are fully pure
Learn from this (a conclusion drawn from a source)

steps.confusionAlert: The כהן is made טמא and then immersed right away. He is pure enough for the פרה but is still a טבול יום, since his sun has not set yet. That detail is the key to the next step.

phrases.english: But with the heifer, we deliberately make him impure,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the כהן who already washed his hands and feet before burning the פרה.

phrases.english: as we learned: they would make impure the priest
who burns the heifer, and immerse him,
to remove the idea from the hearts of the Sadducees

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים: בִּמְעוֹרְבֵי שֶׁמֶשׁ הָיְתָה נַעֲשֵׂית;
phrases.english: who would say: it was done only by those whose sun had set;
phrases.notes: The צדוקים held that a person who immersed must wait for sunset before he could burn the פרה.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: לָא פָּסְלָה בָּהּ (מַחְשֶׁבֶת) טוּמְאָה!
phrases.english: learn from this: impurity does not disqualify it!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. Either way, the point is that impurity does not cancel the washing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof for the open question from before this section: does טומאה cancel קידוש ידים ורגלים?
steps.raayaObject: That טומאה does not cancel a כהן's קידוש ידים ורגלים
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in פרה: the כהן burning the פרה was deliberately made טמא and immersed, and still served

steps.title: The red heifer is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The פרה is different because even a טבול יום may perform it, so we cannot learn from it to other services.
steps.simpleTranslation: The heifer is different, since a person who immersed today is not disqualified for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The פרה follows its own special rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For other services, a טבול יום is not fit to serve. The פרה is unusual because a טבול יום may do it. So a little טומאה not mattering there tells us nothing about regular services.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Since, because
Someone who immersed today but whose sun has not yet set

phrases.english: The heifer is different,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל דִּטְבוּל יוֹם לָא פָּסֵיל בָּהּ.
phrases.english: since a טבול יום is not disqualified for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1 by treating the פרה as an exception.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. The פרה cannot teach about other services.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פרה has a unique leniency (a טבול יום may serve), so its rules about טומאה cannot be applied elsewhere.

steps.title: Then why wash for the heifer at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the פרה is so lenient about purity, why does the כהן need קידוש ידים ורגלים for it at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need him to sanctify his hands and feet?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If purity rules are relaxed for the פרה, the requirement to wash seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said the פרה does not follow regular purity rules. But the כהן still washes his hands and feet for it, which suggests it does follow some Temple rules. The גמרא asks for an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why do I need it?
Sanctifies, meaning washes his hands and feet

phrases.english: If so, why do I need him to sanctify?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the logic of the דחיה in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that the פרה is outside the normal purity rules
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פרה is that lenient, requiring קידוש ידים ורגלים for it seems to have no purpose.

steps.title: The washing makes it resemble Temple service
steps.stepSummary: The washing is required only so that the פרה looks like the regular Temple service, not because it follows all the usual rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: We require it to be done in the style of the Temple service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The washing is there to give the פרה the form of a Temple service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרה does not follow every rule of the inside service, such as the rule against a טבול יום. Still, it must be done in the style of that service, so washing is required. Requiring the washing does not bring in the other purity rules, so the דחיה of step 2 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, in the style of
The Temple service
We require

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the פרה fails. It is a special case where a טבול יום may serve, and its washing is only to make it resemble Temple service. So the question of whether טומאה cancels the washing stays open.

phrases.english: [We require it to be] like the Temple service.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, and they make the sentence complete.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 and keeps the דחיה of step 2 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the purpose of the requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Washing for the פרה must mean it follows the full rules of Temple service.
steps.terutzMaskana: The washing only gives the פרה the look of Temple service. It does not bring in all the other rules.

steps.title: May a priest wash by dipping inside the basin?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: may a כהן do קידוש ידים ורגלים by dipping his hands and feet into the כיור, or must the water come out of it?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: what is the law about sanctifying his hands and feet inside the basin? The Torah said "from it," meaning not inside it. Or perhaps even inside it is fine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand new question about how the washing must be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the כהנים wash "from it" (ממנו). This could mean the water has to come out of the כיור onto the hands, which would rule out dipping. Or it could just mean using the כיור's water in any way, even inside it.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked of them (the חכמים)
The copper basin in the Temple used for washing
From it
Inside it
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Or perhaps

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
What is the law about sanctifying his hands [and feet] in the basin?
phrases.notes: Here "in" means dipping into the water of the כיור itself.

phrases.english: "From it," the Torah said, and not inside it;
or perhaps even inside it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לְקַדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו בַּכִּיּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic within the laws of קידוש ידים ורגלים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether washing by dipping inside the כיור is valid, or whether the water must come out of it

steps.title: A proof from cave water
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק cites a ברייתא: a כהן who immersed in cave water and served has an invalid service. This implies that immersing in the כיור's water in the same way would be valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Come and hear: if he immersed in cave water and served, his service is invalid. This implies that if he used the basin's water the same way as cave water and served, his service is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק tries to answer the new question by reading a ברייתא closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only invalidates the service because the water came from a cave instead of the כיור. That suggests the problem is the source of the water, not the dipping. So dipping into the כיור's own water should be fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersed, dipped
Cave water, meaning water not from the כיור
Similar to, in the same way as
This implies (introduces an inference)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: Come and hear:
or if he immersed in cave water and served,
his service is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: הָא מֵי כִיּוֹר דּוּמְיָא דְּמֵי מְעָרָה, וְעָבַד –
phrases.english: This implies: basin water, used like the cave water, and he served,
his service is valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 5 by inferring from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That dipping hands and feet inside the כיור is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: one who immersed in cave water and served has an invalid service, which implies that dipping into the כיור's water would be valid

steps.title: Cave water was mentioned for a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference from the ברייתא. Cave water had to be mentioned because you might think it is good enough for hands and feet, since it is good enough for the whole body.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ברייתא needed to mention cave water for another reason. Otherwise you might say: if a person may dip his whole body in it, then surely he may dip his hands and feet in it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof from Step 6. The ברייתא mentioned cave water for its own reason, so we cannot learn anything about dipping into the כיור from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 argued that if the ברייתא only rules out cave water, then dipping into the כיור must be fine. The גמרא answers that cave water needed to be singled out because of a strong קל וחומר: water that works for the whole body should surely work for hands and feet. The ברייתא teaches that this is wrong, so the question about dipping into the כיור stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Cave water: water gathered in a cave, kosher for a full-body immersion
It was necessary for him to teach it
So that you should not say (a reason a teaching was needed)
All the more so

steps.confusionAlert: Cave water is fine for immersing the whole body, yet it does not work for קידוש ידים ורגלים. The two washings follow different rules.

phrases.english: No, cave water was necessary for him to mention;
so that you should not say:
his entire body may immerse in it,
so his hands and feet, all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the inference that dipping into the כיור is valid. The ברייתא's ruling about cave water stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא had its own reason to mention cave water: to block a קל וחומר from full-body immersion. So nothing can be inferred about the כיור from it.
steps.whatToRemember: The question from Step 5, whether a כהן may dip his hands and feet into the כיור, is left without a proof.

steps.title: The כיור's water is disqualified at different times for different services
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף rules that the כיור's water expires for each service at the same time that service itself ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף said: The water of the כיור becomes disqualified for the מתירין at the time the מתירין end, and for burning the limbs at the time the limbs end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: when does water left in the כיור stop being usable? רבי חייא בר יוסף links the water's deadline to the service it will be used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Services that 'permit' a קרבן, like sprinkling its blood, can only be done by day, so the water expires for them at sunset. Burning the limbs on the מזבח may go on all night, so the water expires for that at dawn. The water's deadline follows the deadline of the service.

keyTerms.meaning: The water of the כיור, the basin used for washing hands and feet
Become disqualified
Services that allow a קרבן to be eaten or offered, such as sprinkling the blood
Limbs of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling opens a three-way discussion about the כיור's water, and the following steps respond to it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef said:
The water of the Basin becomes disqualified
phrases.notes: He means disqualified just by being left standing in the כיור.

phrases.english: for permitting services, like the permitting services,
phrases.notes: These services are done only by day, so for them the water expires at sunset.

phrases.english: for the limbs, like the limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the כיור after the question of dipping was left unresolved
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כיור's water expires for each service when that service's own time ends: sunset for מתירין, dawn for burning limbs.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the water expires only at dawn for everything
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא disagrees with רבי חייא בר יוסף. Even for the מתירין, the water is disqualified only at dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Even for the מתירין, the water is disqualified only at dawn, just as it is for the limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a different opinion from רבי חייא בר יוסף. For him there is one deadline for all services: dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר יוסף had two deadlines, sunset and dawn. רב חסדא removes the sunset deadline. The water expires only at dawn, even for daytime services like sprinkling blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Dawn, the first light of morning
Even

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
Even for permitting services it does not become disqualified
except at dawn, like the limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי חייא בר יוסף's sunset deadline for מתירין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כיור's water is disqualified only at dawn, for every service.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: once the כיור is sunk, it is not raised again
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that once the כיור has been sunk at the end of the day, it stays down and is not brought back up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Once the כיור has been sunk, it is not raised up again.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion about the כיור: רבי יוחנן says that after it is sunk for the night, it may not be lifted back up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כיור was sunk at night so its water would not be disqualified by being left overnight. רבי יוחנן adds that once this is done, the כיור stays down. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא asks what his rule means for service at night.

keyTerms.meaning: He sank it (lowered the כיור into its pit)
He raises it up

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The Basin, once he has sunk it,
he does not raise it up again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כִּיּוֹר כֵּיוָן שֶׁשִּׁקְּעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third view on the כיור's water, after רבי חייא בר יוסף and רב חסדא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the כיור is sunk, it is not raised again that night.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יוחנן himself allows an unsunk כיור for night service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן's rule means the כיור's water is unfit for night service. It then contradicts that idea with another teaching in רבי יוחנן's name, from אילפא, allowing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean the water is also unfit for the night's service? But רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן, quoting אילפא: If the כיור was not sunk in the evening, a כהן may wash from it for the night's service, but the next day he may not wash from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רבי יוחנן's rule as suggesting the כיור's water cannot be used at night. It then challenges this with a teaching in רבי יוחנן's own name that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule that a sunk כיור may not be raised again seems to imply that water left out after the day ends is unfit even for the night's service. But אילפא, quoted by רבי יוחנן, says an unsunk כיור still works for the night and is disqualified only for the next day. The two teachings in רבי יוחנן's name seem to clash, and the next step resolves this.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? (introduces a doubtful inference)
Night service, such as burning limbs on the מזבח
Fit, usable
Washes hands and feet (does קידוש ידים ורגלים)

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵימְרָא דְּלַעֲבוֹדַת לַיְלָה נָמֵי לָא חֲזֵי?!
phrases.english: Is this to say that it is also unfit for the night's service?!
But didn't Rabbi Asi say,
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Ilfa:
A Basin that he did not sink in the evening,
one may wash from it for the night's service,
and the next day he may not wash from it!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּלַעֲבוֹדַת לַיְלָה נָמֵי לָא חֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what רבי יוחנן's rule seems to imply
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of רבי יוחנן's rule that the כיור's water is unfit for night service
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another teaching in רבי יוחנן's name, from אילפא, says an unsunk כיור may be used for the night's service and is disqualified only the next day. So the implication contradicts רבי יוחנן's own teaching.

steps.title: Not raising the כיור only applies to the day's service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן's 'he does not raise it up' only refers to the day's service. For night service the water is still fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he does not raise it up' mean? It means he does not raise it for the day's service. But for the night's service, the water is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 11 by narrowing what רבי יוחנן meant by 'he does not raise it up.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 it looked like רבי יוחנן said the water is unfit at night, while אילפא quoted him as allowing it. The answer is that 'not raising it up' only refers to using the water for the next day's service. Night service can still use it, so both teachings of רבי יוחנן fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not raise it up (the כיור, after it was sunk)
The daytime service in the בית המקדש
The nighttime service, like burning parts on the מזבח
Fit, usable

phrases.english: What does it mean when he says, 'he does not raise it up'?
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's rule from step 10, about the כיור that was sunk at the end of the day.

phrases.english: For the day's service.
But for the night's service, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11 between two teachings of רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a statement (day service only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He does not raise it up' means the water is unfit for any service after the day ends, including night service.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only means the water is not used for the next day's service. At night it is still fit.

steps.title: Then רבי יוחנן says the same as רבי חייא בר יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that if this is רבי יוחנן's meaning, his view is identical to רבי חייא בר יוסף's.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is the same as the view of רבי חייא בר יוסף!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the answer just given makes רבי יוחנן say exactly what רבי חייא בר יוסף already said. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר יוסף (step 8) said the water expires for each service when that service ends: for day service at sunset, for night service at dawn. The reading of רבי יוחנן in step 12 says the same thing. So why does רבי יוחנן's statement need to be taught as a separate rule?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
This is the same as

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: This is the same as the view of רבי חייא בר יוסף!
phrases.notes: See step 8: each service's water expires when that service's time ends.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי הַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 12 by showing it makes רבי יוחנן's rule a repeat of רבי חייא בר יוסף's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רבי יוחנן given in step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'not raising' refers only to the day's service, while night service can still use the water, then רבי יוחנן adds nothing new beyond רבי חייא בר יוסף's rule.
